ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Charlotte Brontë

code.originalText: Prenatal visit at 17 weeks: nausea and vomiting review and thyroid recheck

text.paragraph: Ms. Brontë returns at 17 weeks 1 day. She has not vomited for ten days and has needed no ondansetron for two weeks. Mild nausea comes on only when she is tired. She eats well and walks out most afternoons. She takes doxylamine-pyridoxine four tablets a day, aspirin 81 mg at bedtime without bruising or bleeding, and folic acid. Her PUQE-24 score is 4. She has no palpitations, headache, visual change, pain, bleeding, or urinary symptoms. She is writing most mornings and feels hopeful. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-24; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Fundus midway between the pubic bone and the umbilicus
Fetal heart 150 per minute by Doppler
First pregnancy at 38 (elderly primigravida), single live intrauterine pregnancy dated by ultrasound at 7 weeks 1 day
S — Synthetic modern prenatal care anchored to the documented report that she was pregnant when she died; the pregnancy itself is questioned in one source (CLM-0019).
Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, moderate (PUQE-24 score 10), with early weight loss, under evaluation for hyperemesis gravidarum

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the hyperemesis gravidarum diagnosis at the sick visit; her documented "perpetual nausea" is D and the hyperemesis reading of it is R.

Hyperemesis gravidarum with metabolic disturbance: unable to keep fluids down, 7.4 percent weight loss, dehydration, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypochloremic alkalosis, low magnesium, and raised transaminases; PUQE-24 score 14
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented final illness and the retrospective hyperemesis interpretation; it is not asserted as her historical diagnosis.
Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis: suppressed TSH and mildly raised free T4 with hyperemesis, no goiter, eye signs, or tremor; no treatment needed
S — Synthetic finding that teaches the thyroid tests in hyperemesis; it echoes no documented illness.

list.item:
Hyperemesis gravidarum, settled (O21.1). PUQE-24 score 4 and weight 46.2 kg, back above her pre-pregnancy weight. Hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL. [S]
Ondansetron stopped.
Taper doxylamine-pyridoxine over two weeks: three tablets a day for a week, then two at bedtime for a week, then stop; restart at the last dose that worked if vomiting returns.
Call if vomiting returns and she cannot keep fluids down.

Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis, resolved (O99.281). TSH 0.92 mIU/L and free T4 1.1 ng/dL: normal as hCG has fallen; no treatment was needed. [S]
No further thyroid tests unless symptoms develop.

First pregnancy at 38 (O09.519). Fetal heart 150 per minute; blood pressure 108/68 mmHg on aspirin. EPDS 5 with item 10 scored 0. [S]
Continue aspirin 81 mg at bedtime and folic acid; restart the iron-containing prenatal vitamin now that nausea has settled.
Detailed anatomy scan in three weeks.
Glucose challenge test at 24 to 28 weeks; Tdap at 27 to 36 weeks; repeat mood screen in the third trimester.

list.item: Nausea and vomiting mild (PUQE-24 score 6 or less) and weight back to her pre-pregnancy 46.0 kg by about 17 weeks. Outcome by 2026-03-24: PUQE-24 score 4 and weight 46.2 kg at 17 weeks 1 day [S]

Hydration and electrolytes normal within two weeks of any admission. Outcome by 2026-02-10: Sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, magnesium, phosphate, and transaminases all normal nine days after discharge [S]

An informed choice about aneuploidy screening and diagnostic testing by 13 weeks. Outcome by 2026-02-24: Chose cell-free DNA screening (low risk) and the nuchal translucency scan (1.5 mm); declined diagnostic testing [S]
Low-dose aspirin started between 12 and 16 weeks if indicated. Outcome by 2026-02-24: Started at 13 weeks 1 day for two moderate risk factors [S]
Tuberculosis screening completed and explained by the second visit. Outcome by 2026-01-20: Interferon-gamma release assay negative; no latent infection; no chest radiograph needed [S]
Mood screened in each trimester, with support offered. Outcome by 2026-03-24: PHQ-9 5 at intake, EPDS 9 after the admission and 5 at 17 weeks; item 10 scored 0 each time [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 189: Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy (2018); The Management of Nausea and Vomiting in Pregnancy and Hyperemesis Gravidarum (Green-top Guideline No. 69) (2024); Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive Medication (2021); 2017 Guidelines of the American Thyroid Association for the Diagnosis and Management of Thyroid Disease During Pregnancy and the Postpartum (2017); Screening and Diagnosis of Mental Health Conditions During Pregnancy and Postpartum (Clinical Practice Guideline No. 4) (2023)
Follow-up: Anatomy scan in three weeks and prenatal visit in four weeks. [S]
